hero.headline: I build fast,
hero.bio: I'm Michael Quispe, Software Developer focused on performance and scalable architectures. Motorsport enthusiast (BMW M, F1, WEC) and Sim Racing fan — where precision, telemetry, and every millisecond matter, just like in code.

stack.title: STACK
stack.description: Tuned by language, optimized for purpose. Each tool chosen for the terrain.

finance-app.title: Financial Simulator
finance-app.description: Web platform for credit and real estate financing simulation. Implements a custom engine for real-time cash flow, rate (TCEA), and amortization calculations, with cloud persistence.
highlights: Complex financial logic isolated in independent calculation modules
Server-side routing architecture with Next.js and Turbopack
Authentication and NoSQL database integration via Firebase
finance-app.problem: Generic spreadsheets and simulators cannot model real mortgage loans with variable rates, grace periods, and precise amortizations. A platform delivering verifiable and reproducible results was needed.
finance-app.role: Full-stack Developer · Technical design and calculation engine construction.

decisions.title: Isolated calculation engine
decisions.body: All financial logic (TCEA, cash flow, amortization) lives in pure modules with no UI or I/O dependencies. This enables isolated algorithm testing and reuse across server and client.

decisions.title: Next.js with App Router
decisions.body: Server-side routing and server components to reduce client-side JS. Turbopack in dev for fast iteration.

decisions.title: Firebase as backend
decisions.body: Auth + Firestore for persistence. Chose a BaaS to focus time on the financial domain rather than infrastructure.

challenges.title: Numerical precision
challenges.body: Financial calculations don't tolerate floating-point errors. Operations were normalized to fixed-point arithmetic to avoid drift across long amortization schedules.

challenges.title: Reactivity on long schedules
challenges.body: Recalculating 360 installments on every input change stalled the render. The engine was memoized and non-critical updates deferred.

oncontrol-telemedicine.title: OnControl — Telemedicine
oncontrol-telemedicine.description: Mobile app for medical follow-up, appointment scheduling, and treatment control. Connects doctors and patients through a structured system for symptom and procedure tracking.
highlights: Strict Clean Architecture implementation (Domain, Data, Presentation)
Reactive state management and dependency injection
Smooth native UI compiled for Android and iOS
oncontrol-telemedicine.problem: Medical follow-up fragmented across WhatsApp, calls, and paper causes errors in chronic treatments. A single channel between patient and doctor with full traceability was required.
oncontrol-telemedicine.role: Mobile Developer · Layer architecture and presentation modules.

decisions.title: Strict Clean Architecture
decisions.body: Three layers (Domain, Data, Presentation) with unidirectional dependency. The domain knows nothing about Flutter or Firebase, allowing backend swaps without touching business rules.

decisions.title: BLoC for state
decisions.body: Predictable, testable reactive states. Each feature has its own decoupled BLoC.

decisions.title: Dependency injection
decisions.body: Central Service Locator to build dependency graphs. Enables mock-based testing and keeps widgets agnostic of the data layer.

challenges.title: Offline-first sync
challenges.body: Patients register symptoms without connectivity. A local queue was designed to reconcile with the backend on reconnect, preventing duplicates.

challenges.title: UX for two distinct roles
challenges.body: Doctor and patient share the codebase but see opposite flows. A role-based router was built to mount only the relevant modules per session.
